 Photo by: Tim Cowie Beck, Chen & McMyler to Open LPGA Final Qualifying Thursday
 11/18/2026 10:00:00 AM | Women's Golf
 Scoring Share: MOBILE, Ala.  – Three former Duke women's golfers – Laetitia Beck , Anne Chen and Emma McMyler – will compete in the Final Qualifying Stage of LPGA Q-Series Nov. 19-23 at Magnolia Grove Golf Course in Mobile, Alabama.
The Blue Devil trio will join a 115-player field competing for LPGA Tour status for the 2027 season. The tournament will feature 90 holes of stroke play with a cut following the fourth round. Competitors will play two rounds each on the Falls and Crossings courses before the final round on the Crossings Course. The top 25 golfers and ties will earn LPGA Tour status for 2027.
McMyler advanced through the Qualifying Stage earlier this month at Plantation Golf and Country Club in Venice, Florida. She registered rounds of 77, 68, 69 and 73 for a 1-under-par 287 to finish tied for 52nd and secure her place in the final stage.
A native of San Antonio, Texas, McMyler made 13 starts and seven cuts during her rookie LPGA Tour season in 2026, earning $50,934. Her results included a tie for 40th at the ShopRite LPGA Classic and a tie for 43rd at the LOTTE Championship presented by Hoakalei.
McMyler received honorable mention All-America recognition from Golfweek and the Women's Golf Coaches Association in 2023-24 with the Blue Devils. She finished the season ranked No. 38 nationally with a team-best 72.03 stroke average and graduated from Duke's Fuqua School of Business with a Master of Management Studies degree in May 2024.
Beck's 2026 LPGA Tour campaign featured a tie for 14th at the ShopRite LPGA Classic, where she opened with an 8-under-par 63 to take the first-round lead. She finished the tournament with a 3-under-par 210 and was paired in the final round with former Duke teammate Celine Boutier , who went on to claim the title.
A 2014 Duke graduate, Beck helped lead the Blue Devils to the 2014 NCAA Championship. She earned All-America honors in 2013 and 2014, was a four-time All-ACC selection and received ACC Rookie of the Year recognition in 2011. Beck returned to the LPGA Tour in 2026 following a successful Epson Tour campaign that included her first professional victory at the 2025 Atlantic Beach Classic.
Chen has competed on both the LPGA and Epson tours in 2026. Her LPGA results were highlighted by a tie for 14th at the Standard Portland Classic, where she carded rounds of 74, 65, 70 and 66 for a 13-under-par 275. During the final round, she registered her first professional hole-in-one on the par-3 eighth hole with a 9-iron from 134 yards.
A native of Sugar Land, Texas, Chen earned her first professional victory at the 2025 Epson Tour Championship, winning on the fifth playoff hole after finishing regulation at 22-under-par 266. The victory secured her LPGA Tour membership for 2026.
Chen graduated from Duke in 2024 with a degree in public policy and earned All-ACC honors in 2022.
